title: ExtExactFunctorIdentityComparison
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] with small Ext groups [def-pc-ext], $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ an additive functor preserving finite limits and finite colimits, and $e:F\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal A}$ a natural isomorphism. For objects $A,B\in\mathcal A$, $n\geq0$, and $x\in\operatorname{Ext}^n_{\mathcal A}(A,B)$, use the termwise exact functor on derived categories [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to define $F_*x$. Write $\operatorname{mk}_0(a)$ for the degree-zero Ext class of a morphism $a$. Then
$$\operatorname{mk}_0(e_B)\circ F_*x=x\circ\operatorname{mk}_0(e_A).$$

source.place: Lemma Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), parts (3)-(4), and Definition Tag 06XQ (definition-ext); argument by naturality on localized complexes, written by K1

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], F acts termwise on complexes and preserves quasi-isomorphisms, so induces a functor on their localization. The termwise identity functor localizes to the identity, and e induces a natural isomorphism from the induced F to the identity. This follows from the localization universal property [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The components of this isomorphism commute with shifts because e acts termwise.

Under [def-pc-ext], x is a morphism A[0] to B[0][n]. Apply naturality of the localized e to x. The source component is mk_0(e_A), the target component is mk_0(e_B)[n], and the identity functor leaves x unchanged. This gives exactly the asserted equality.

lean.statement:
theorem exactFunctorIdentityComparison
    {C : Type*} [Category C] [Abelian C] [HasExt.{w} C]
    (F : C ⥤ C) [F.Additive]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits F] [PreservesFiniteColimits F]
    (e : F ≅ 𝟭 C) {X Y : C} {n : ℕ} (x : Ext.{w} X Y n) :
    (x.mapExactFunctor F).comp (Ext.mk₀ (e.hom.app Y)) (add_zero n) =
      (Ext.mk₀ (e.hom.app X)).comp x (zero_add n)
